elements.text: WayFinder

Campus Navigation Guide
Project Title Finalisation
Presented by: Project Team
B.Tech Project Presentation 2026

Why campus navigation is difficult

• New students and visitors do not know where buildings are located
• Asking for directions takes time and creates confusion
• Important details such as timings are scattered
Introduction

How WayFinder helps

• Search a place by name or category
• View campus locations on an interactive map
• Receive a simple walking route to the destination
Project Title Finalisation

Why “WayFinder – Campus Navigation Guide”

• “WayFinder” clearly describes the purpose of guiding users
• “Campus Navigation Guide” defines the project scope
• The title is short, easy to remember, and suitable for a college project

Project focus

Campus locations, search, map-based discovery, and simple navigation directions for students, parents, faculty, and visitors.
Literature Survey and Existing System

Common approaches

• Printed campus maps
• Static map images on websites
• General navigation applications

Our learning

A campus guide should combine location data, search, map markers, and easy directions in one place

Observed limitations

• Printed maps become outdated
• Static images cannot filter or search locations
• General maps often miss campus-specific facilities and timings
Objectives

Location discovery

Help users find important campus places quickly

Interactive map

Show buildings with markers and clear details

Simple navigation

Generate distance, walking time, and written steps
Problem Statement

Users

New students, parents, visitors, faculty, and event participants need quick guidance.

Challenge

Campus information is hard to find when maps are incomplete or directions depend on asking others.

Need

A simple web application that finds a place, shows it on a map, and gives navigation guidance.
Proposed System

Frontend

• React and Vite interface
• Leaflet map with OpenStreetMap tiles
• Search, filters, route display, and toast notifications

Backend

• FastAPI REST APIs
• SQLite database for locations and contact messages
• SQLAlchemy models with request validation
Key features: location details, category filtering, walking estimate, and contact form
Methodology
1. Collect campus location details
2. Store data in SQLite
3. Serve data through FastAPI
4. Display map and route in React
The development approach keeps the project modular: the frontend consumes REST APIs, and the backend manages location and contact data.
Expected Outcomes

Fast search

Users can locate Library, Hostel, Canteen, Parking, and other key places.

Clear map view

Markers and popups make the campus easier to understand.

Simple route guidance

Users see distance, estimated walking time, and written directions.
Future Scope

Live location

Use the device location to show the user’s current position.

Student login

Save favourite places and frequently used routes.

Accessible routes

Add wheelchair-friendly paths and accessibility information.

Campus updates

Allow staff to update events, closures, and building timings.
